task_summary: Define the interface contract for the 'Project Scaffold & Configuration' component (id: project_scaffold). This component initializes the exemplar-tools-doc/ project directory with all configuration files: package.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts (port 4000), tailwind.config.ts, postcss.config.ts, index.html, vercel.json (SPA rewrite), and vitest.setup.ts. All files must be TypeScript — no .py or .js source files. The contract must specify exact file paths, file contents structure, dependency versions, and configuration shapes so downstream components (app_routing, shared_components, page_components) can rely on a deterministic project structure.

findings.finding: The canonical Vite React-TS template places config at root (vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, tsconfig.node.json), source under src/, and index.html at root. vite.config.ts uses defineConfig from 'vite' and @vitejs/plugin-react. The dev server port is set via server.port in the Vite config. TypeScript strict mode should be enabled. Path aliases (e.g., @/ → src/) are commonly configured in both vite.config.ts (via resolve.alias) and tsconfig.json (via paths).
findings.source: Vite official documentation (vitejs.dev), create-vite template react-ts
findings.relevance: Directly defines the structure and configuration patterns this component must produce.

findings.topic: Tailwind CSS v3/v4 with Vite — TypeScript config
findings.finding: Tailwind CSS v3 uses a tailwind.config.ts (or .js) file with content paths pointing to src/**/*.{ts,tsx}. PostCSS config is required — postcss.config.ts (or .mjs) must reference tailwindcss and autoprefixer plugins. Tailwind v3's config exports a Config type from 'tailwindcss/types/config' (or 'tailwindcss' directly). A globals.css with @tailwind base/components/utilities directives is needed as the CSS entry point.
findings.source: Tailwind CSS v3 documentation, Vite integration guide
findings.relevance: Tailwind and PostCSS config files are explicit deliverables of this component. Using .ts for both avoids .js files per project rules.

findings.finding: PostCSS does NOT natively support .ts config files. The standard approach is postcss.config.mjs (ESM) or postcss.config.cjs (CJS). Vite's internal PostCSS loader reads postcss.config.js/.cjs/.mjs but not .ts. However, since Vite processes PostCSS internally, the postcss config can alternatively be inlined into vite.config.ts via the css.postcss option, avoiding a separate config file entirely. This is the cleanest way to satisfy the 'no .js files' constraint.
findings.source: Vite docs (css.postcss config option), PostCSS loader documentation
findings.relevance: Critical — the operating procedures mandate no .js source files. postcss.config.ts is not natively supported. Two viable paths: inline in vite.config.ts or use .mjs extension.

findings.finding: Vitest is configured either in a dedicated vitest.config.ts or within vite.config.ts via the test property (using /// <reference types='vitest' /> or mergeConfig). The setup file (vitest.setup.ts) should import '@testing-library/jest-dom' to extend expect matchers. The test environment must be set to 'jsdom'. setupFiles should point to the setup file path. globals: true enables global test functions (describe, it, expect) without imports.
findings.relevance: vitest.setup.ts is an explicit deliverable. The test configuration must be correct for all downstream component tests.

findings.finding: Recommended tsconfig for Vite React-TS: target ES2020+, module ESNext, moduleResolution bundler (TS 5+) or node, jsx react-jsx, strict true, skipLibCheck true, esModuleInterop true, isolatedModules true (required by Vite's esbuild transform), lib [ES2020, DOM, DOM.Iterable]. A separate tsconfig.node.json is used for vite.config.ts with composite: true. The main tsconfig references it and uses include: ['src'].
findings.source: Vite create-vite react-ts template, TypeScript handbook
findings.relevance: tsconfig.json is an explicit deliverable. isolatedModules is especially important — Vite requires it and omitting it causes subtle transpilation bugs.

findings.finding: vercel.json for SPAs uses { "rewrites": [{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html" }] }. This catches all routes and serves index.html, enabling client-side routing. The exact shape is specified in the task description. No buildCommand or outputDirectory is strictly needed if Vercel auto-detects the Vite framework.
findings.source: Vercel documentation on rewrites, SPA deployment guides
findings.relevance: vercel.json is an explicit deliverable with exact content specified in the task.

findings.finding: For reproducibility, dependencies should use caret ranges (^) with specific minor versions rather than 'latest'. Key version considerations: react 18.x (react 19 is canary), react-router-dom v6 (v7 has breaking changes with new data router API), tailwindcss v3.4.x (v4 has breaking config changes), vite v5.x, vitest v1.x or v2.x (should match vite major), prism-react-renderer v2.x (v1 had very different API). The 'type: module' field in package.json is recommended for ESM Vite projects.
findings.relevance: package.json is a core deliverable. Version mismatches between vite and vitest, or using Tailwind v4 config format with v3 expectations, are common pitfalls.

findings.finding:
Vite uses index.html at the project root as the entry point (not in public/). It must contain a
mount point and a entry. The HTML should include proper meta viewport tag, charset, and title. CSS is imported from within the TS entry point, not linked in HTML.
findings.source: Vite documentation on index.html and project structure
findings.relevance: index.html is an explicit deliverable. Placing it in the wrong directory or omitting type='module' on the script tag are common mistakes.

findings.topic: TypeScript path aliases for clean imports
findings.finding: Path aliases like @/ → ./src/ improve import readability. Must be configured in BOTH tsconfig.json (paths: { '@/*': ['./src/*'] }, baseUrl: '.') AND vite.config.ts (resolve.alias: { '@': path.resolve(__dirname, 'src') }). Without both, either the IDE or the build will fail to resolve. With vitest, aliases from vite.config.ts are automatically inherited.
findings.source: Vite resolve.alias docs, TypeScript path mapping docs
findings.relevance: While not explicitly required, path aliases are a strong convention for projects of this scale. If included, dual-configuration is essential.

findings.topic: Vitest type augmentation for jest-dom matchers
findings.finding: With @testing-library/jest-dom v6+, TypeScript types are included in the package. The setup file needs `import '@testing-library/jest-dom'` for runtime, and tsconfig should include the setup file or use a triple-slash reference `/// <reference types='@testing-library/jest-dom' />` for type coverage. Without this, matchers like toBeInTheDocument() will show TS errors.
findings.source: @testing-library/jest-dom v6 migration guide, vitest TypeScript docs
findings.relevance: Downstream tests will use jest-dom matchers extensively. Type augmentation must be correct in the scaffold.

findings.finding: With jsx: 'react-jsx' in tsconfig (the new JSX transform), explicit `import React from 'react'` is NOT required by the compiler for JSX. However, the project operating procedures explicitly mandate it: 'Every .tsx file must include import React from react at the top'. This is a project convention that must be respected regardless of compiler settings.
findings.source: Project operating procedures, React 17+ new JSX transform docs
findings.relevance: The scaffold's tsconfig uses react-jsx which doesn't need the import, but the operating procedures override this. All downstream .tsx files must include the import. The scaffold should not configure anything that breaks this pattern.

findings.topic: CSS entry point for Tailwind in Vite
findings.finding: A src/index.css (or src/globals.css) file with the three Tailwind directives (@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;) must exist and be imported in the application entry point (main.tsx). This file is the bridge between Tailwind's PostCSS processing and the application. Without it, Tailwind classes have no effect.
findings.relevance: This is an often-forgotten file in scaffold definitions. Without it, the entire Tailwind integration is non-functional even if all config files are correct.

recommended_approach:
The project_scaffold component should produce a deterministic set of files at known paths under the project root. The interface contract should:

1. **Enumerate every file path** as a literal string union or checklist — downstream components depend on exact paths (e.g., `src/main.tsx`, `src/index.css`).

2. **Inline PostCSS config into vite.config.ts** via the `css.postcss` option rather than producing a standalone postcss.config.ts, since PostCSS does not natively support .ts config files. If a standalone file is required per the task description, use postcss.config.mjs (ESM) as the .ts-equivalent — this satisfies "no .js" while remaining functional.

3. **Configure vitest inside vite.config.ts** using the `test` property with `environment: 'jsdom'`, `globals: true`, and `setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts']`. The setup file imports `@testing-library/jest-dom`.

4. **Pin dependency versions** to known-compatible ranges: react@^18.3, react-dom@^18.3, react-router-dom@^6.23, vite@^5.4, @vitejs/plugin-react@^4.3, tailwindcss@^3.4, vitest@^1.6 (or ^2.0), @testing-library/react@^16, @testing-library/jest-dom@^6, jsdom@^24, prism-react-renderer@^2.3.

5. **Set Vite dev server port to 4000** explicitly in `server.port`.

6. **vercel.json** with the exact SPA rewrite rule as specified.

7. **Include src/index.css** with Tailwind directives and **src/main.tsx** as a minimal React entry point that imports the CSS and mounts to `#root`.

8. **Export a ProjectManifest type** from the contract that enumerates all produced file paths, enabling downstream components to assert scaffold completeness.

9. **Contract tests** should verify: (a) all expected file paths exist, (b) package.json contains all required dependencies, (c) vite.config.ts has port 4000, (d) vitest.setup.ts imports jest-dom, (e) vercel.json has the correct rewrite rule, (f) no .py or .js files exist in the output.
alternatives_considered: Standalone postcss.config.ts: Not viable — PostCSS loader doesn't support .ts. Would require tsx or ts-node as a runtime dependency, adding unnecessary complexity.
postcss.config.mjs as standalone file: Viable and explicit. Satisfies 'no .js' rule since .mjs is a distinct extension. Preferred if the task requires a visible standalone file.
Inline PostCSS in vite.config.ts: Cleanest solution, avoids the .js problem entirely, but deviates from the task description which lists postcss.config.ts as a separate file.

Vitest in separate vitest.config.ts: Adds another config file. Since Vitest inherits from Vite config, co-locating via the test property in vite.config.ts is simpler and ensures alias/plugin consistency.
Tailwind v4 (CSS-first config): Breaking change from v3 config format. The task implies v3 patterns (tailwind.config.ts with content array). Stick with v3.4.x.
react-router-dom v7: Major breaking changes (framework mode, data routers as default). v6.x is stable and matches the simple SPA routing pattern needed here.
risks: PostCSS .ts config: postcss.config.ts will silently fail to load in Vite. Must use .mjs or inline in vite.config.ts. This is the highest-risk item since the task description explicitly names postcss.config.ts.
Vite/Vitest version mismatch: vitest major version should align with vite major version. A mismatch (e.g., vitest@2 with vite@5) can cause plugin incompatibilities.
Tailwind v3 vs v4 confusion: If tailwindcss@^4 is installed, the tailwind.config.ts format is completely different (CSS-first). Must pin to ^3.4.
Missing src/index.css with Tailwind directives: If omitted, Tailwind classes render nothing. Easy to forget since it's not a 'config file' per se.
react-router-dom v7 auto-install: If no version pin is specified, npm may install v7 which has a fundamentally different API. Must pin to ^6.
@testing-library/jest-dom type augmentation: Without proper type setup, all jest-dom matchers (toBeInTheDocument, toHaveClass, etc.) will show TypeScript errors in downstream tests.

import React from 'react' convention: tsconfig jsx: 'react-jsx' makes this import unnecessary for compilation, but the project mandates it. Must not configure anything (like a linter rule) that strips this import.
Missing type: 'module' in package.json: Vite ESM projects should set this; without it, some imports may fail or behave unexpectedly.
compliance_notes: All output files must be .ts/.tsx — no .py or .js. postcss.config must be .mjs or inlined.
Implementation language is TypeScript — contract types, config files, and all source must be TypeScript.
Named exports required on all types, interfaces, functions, and constants.
Every .tsx file must import React from 'react' at the top.
vitest + @testing-library/react in jsdom environment — must be configured correctly in scaffold.
import.meta.env.VITE_X must be used directly — no (import.meta as any) casts.
Prefer stdlib over third-party libraries — only install the explicitly listed dependencies.
All functions must have at least one test; tests must run without external services.
String keys in maps must be verified against source of truth (type registry), not inferred.
